newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's trade with Israel worth $18 million.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's trade with Israel worth $18 million.

text.p: Jordan and Israel traded goods worth $18 million in the second half of 1996 after opening their border to cargo last June for the first time in nearly 50 years, according to official statistics released on Tuesday.
They indicated the initial balance of trade between the former foes weighed heavily in Israel's favour, with Israeli exports worth $12.25 million compared to $5.75 million from Jordan.

The statistics, issued by Jordan's Trade Ministry and the Israeli embassy, showed that 1,042 Jordanian trucks delivered cargo to the northern crossing point against 1,056 Israeli trailers that discharged Jordan-bound goods.
Another 259 Jordanian trucks offloaded goods for Israel at the southern border crossing near Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba against 35 in the opposite direction.

Jordan last year reached a long-delayed transport accord that was essential to boost trade after their 1994 peace treaty. But until late last year all goods had to be taken off trucks on one side of the border and re-loaded on the other side under a time-consuming system known as "back-to-back".
Jordanian officials say the back-to-back system, and Israeli security restrictions, hampered the flow of goods.

Cross border trade is however expected to rise in 1997 with the implementation of a "door-to-door" system where goods are taken directly to their final destination, eliminating logistical and bureaucratic obstacles.
However the new system will take time to come fully into effect, officials say.

Israel's trade officials estimate the overall trade could reach between $50 million to $100 million this year alone with progress in Middle East peace encouraging more Jordanians to do business with the Jewish state.
Israel exported a total of $12.25 million to Jordan, of which around $4 million worth of goods were transit from Europe through Israel's Mediterranean ports to Jordan.
Among the main items Israel exported to Jordan were machinery, chemicals and agricultural plants.
Jordanian exports to Israel reached $5.75 million, mostly textiles, Israeli embassy figures show.
